layout.identity: stable metadata id; folder path is not identity
rules: Each work folder has one index.yaml node; index is the node, not an extra directory listing.

Split by responsibility as needed: business, architecture, backend, frontend and uat each own nodes. Business can split into rules, journeys and acceptance; FE into draw/code; UAT into flows. Names and depth are flexible, not mandatory scaffolding.
A leaf has requirements, assertions and state. A parent keeps scope and derives progress from required children, never authored state/completion.

Extend existing nodes and preserve stable IDs, assets and evidence. New required work prevents parent done; unrelated completed branches remain intact. Scope or source changes invalidate only affected proof.
Several workflows may target the same work nodes; no duplicated business tree per run. Local workflow tracking is ignored by validation/digests and Git.
Declare semantic design/source files using node.assets with paths under own assets/. Their actual bytes contribute to node input binding.

Record output screenshots/videos in evidence assets with scope: node and paths under the primary owner assets/. Output evidence is not also declared as a semantic input, avoiding self-invalidating proof.
Source code remains in bound repositories; code/index.yaml tracks requirements, exact source references and completion.
Legacy node.yaml/node.md remains read compatibility; exactly one node file per work folder. Do not automatically migrate existing user work.

gates.approvalTrust: Receipts must come from actual user messages. This local validator binds receipts but cannot authenticate a human; the coordinator must never fabricate approvals.

workflows.when: Create/revise a visual direction, implement FE and verify its accepted UX flows.
Reconstruct Work from selected existing source/worktrees and resolve business/architecture.
Create a new Work purpose and deliver business plus architecture.
Design, implement and independently accept a bounded backend API.
Publish and deploy a verified delivery only when both effects are selected.
Deliver exactly three independent BE/FE/UAT pieces with disjoint mutable scope.
Complete one ad hoc job from the request; small fixes, standalone deployments or data corrections may use this workflow.
Create or bind the missing Work workspace within the original request scope, then resume the suspended workflow after user approval.

operators.goal: Resolve a bounded design into real repository ownership, contracts and implementable code scope.

action.en: Research exact FE/BE revisions, manifests, entrypoints, DI, API handlers, data stores, jobs, deploy topology and tests. Follow inbound callers and outbound consumers; cite repository/path/symbol/revision and distinguish observed paths from proposed paths. Trace each network hop from caller symbol through URL/config resolution, proxy/ingress wiring, receiving handler and deployment owner; record synchronous, async and in-process edges separately. Names and comments are clues, not endpoint proof. Keep observed and desired routing separate and block contradictory boundary decisions. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers.

Map accepted business flow and AC IDs to responsible services and authoritative data writers. Draw the logical request/response and asynchronous event sequence in ordered flow rows, including trust boundaries; never assume a class is an independently deployed service. Write ordered serviceCalls with caller/callee service IDs, caller/receiver source refs, operation, endpoint binding, credentials/trust boundary, data classification, timeout/retry and evidence status. Verify response path and downstream side effects. Unobserved deployment/runtime facts remain unknown.

Choose and justify the smallest design meeting hard constraints, comparing alternatives where material. Specify API request/response/errors, compatibility, transaction, lock scope, idempotency, event ordering, retry limits, timeout, compensation and read-back. Unknowns stay explicit. Evaluate Saga, CQRS, transactional outbox/inbox, idempotency, concurrency control and resilience patterns against actual invariants. Each pattern decision says adopt/preserve/reject/defer, why, simpler alternative, trade-off, scope and proof. Saga requires participant-local transactions, durable orchestration/choreography state, compensation/pivot/retry and failure recovery; an outbox alone is not Saga. CQRS requires explicit read/write models and consistency/read-your-writes policy; separate handler filenames do not prove CQRS and CQRS does not require event sourcing or separate databases.

Write codeImpacts with exact repository/path/symbol, observed/proposed identity, direct/transitive relation, change/preserve/review decision, reason, caller chain, tests and protected paths. Write serviceImpacts with deployable owner, inbound/outbound consumers, stores/events, compatibility, rollout/rollback and observability; explain unaffected boundaries. Map every selected pattern and service call back to exact source symbols, data/event schemas, deployment/config owners and protected paths. Do not route traffic to a different service merely because its repository contains a matching resolver.

Review each trust boundary: authentication, object/tenant authorization, validation, credential custody, sensitive logs, external provider/AI input, replay and resource abuse where relevant. Link threat, server-side control owner, code/service impact and positive/negative AC. Record residual risks and decision owner without claiming a security audit ran. Add a threat model per trust boundary: assets, entry points, attacker capability, exploit path, impact, prevention/detection, control owner and negative acceptance. Assess object/function/property authorization, tenant isolation, token issuer/audience/scope and forwarding, SSRF/redirect/DNS/egress, injection, webhook authenticity/replay, resource/AI cost abuse, sensitive transcripts/logs and dependency risks when applicable. Mark non-applicability with evidence; unresolved high-impact risks need a decision owner and block acceptance.

Produce implementation ceilings, protected paths, dependencies and required checks from actual repository scripts/CI. Lint, typecheck, tests/coverage, build and Sonar execute inside FE/BE implement; this op specifies them only. Bind rollout/migration/cleanup plans without executing them. Preserve business expected results unchanged. Design failure-injection tests for wrong service target, unauthorized forwarding, stale reads, duplicate/out-of-order messages, crash after commit before publish, compensation failure and retry exhaustion as applicable; implementations run them. Author canonical user journeys and journeyCoverage links to flow/AC IDs using the shared journey contract; preserve accepted journeys unchanged in architecture. Do not convert internal service hops into UI actions. Browser-free scope may use an empty array only when no UAT acceptance is assigned. Partition the selected FE/BE code impacts into cohesive implementation pieces with exact paths, protected boundaries, prerequisites, acceptance IDs, safe commit boundaries and test ownership. Check that each operation is assigned once; pieces may run in parallel only with disjoint mutable ownership and no dependency on another piece output.

Validate .work and requirement→flow→code/service→security→AC coverage. Write the JSON specification into extensions.work3.specification before review digest, with actual source-map/review evidence. Output code/service impact, contracts, security controls and verification plan to backend/FE implement; unresolved required ownership/compatibility decisions block handoff. No secondary is defined; do not invent calls. Design completion does not complete implementation or UAT. Require serviceCalls, patternDecisions and securityReview JSON and reject unresolved routing/pattern/security blockers before handoff. Record documentation citations separately from source evidence; a passing structural validator cannot prove a deployed endpoint or security control. When selected in a job matrix, produce E/job-result.json bound to the exact request, its output schema and every required criterion. This handoff is conditional and does not change standalone or named frontend response contracts.

operators.goal: Implement one selected backend outcome and prove its declared contract on actual code.

action.en: Bind the exact operation/AC set and inspect existing code plus sibling conventions, including DI/module registration and every relevant caller. Reuse already conforming behavior. Own preparation through delivery: inspect readiness and reproduce the requested defect when applicable, partition the selected work into cohesive changes and check callers before editing. Resolve repository-local dependencies and bounded development runtime needs under the existing scope. Shared library changes belong to the actual FE or BE package owner: include owner tests, packaging/export compatibility and selected consumer integration proof in this same implementation; never publish a package implicitly. Keep shared paths exclusive and report a missing required external authority rather than inventing a helper. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers.
Implement transport, validation, permission checks, use-case logic and persistence inside the declared ownership. Enforce denials before unauthorized side effects; do not invent fallback behavior.
Implement declared transaction, retry/idempotency, concurrency, error identity and read-time revalidation. Migrations are source only; applying them remotely is not included.

Add/repair scoped tests; execute positive, denial, invalid-input and applicable race/reload regressions plus repository-required checks. Preserve raw failure and no-test/not-run status; repair only within this approved implementation goal. This implement op owns lint, typecheck, relevant tests/coverage, affected builds and Sonar. Resolve real repository scripts and CI thresholds; record command, source tree/commit, result and sanitized logs. For Sonar record the analysis/revision and actual server quality-gate result after processing; scanner submission alone is not pass. Fix scoped failures and rerun affected checks. A missing runner, token reference, coverage target or unavailable required Sonar gate is blocked/not-run, never pass; do not move this responsibility to architecture, business or UAT. Reuse existing authorization and keep secrets outside evidence.

Review diff, verify no unrelated changes, commit the piece when authorized and read back the real SHA/diff. Bind proof to actual tested bytes; fresh code needs fresh required evidence. Stop after delivery. Create the scoped local commit under the existing implementation authority after required checks pass, read back full SHA and committed diff, and return per-repository commit references. Preserve unrelated local changes; never stage everything, bypass hooks, push or invent an empty commit. If no code changed, return the verified existing commit and explain no change. Missing commit proof prevents a passing delivery. When selected in a job matrix, produce E/job-result.json bound to the exact request, its output schema and every required criterion. This handoff is conditional and does not change standalone or named frontend response contracts. For an explicitly requested running API handoff, verify the actual owned development runtime and produce api-contract.json and runtime.json for FE/API acceptance; missing required served proof blocks that handoff.

operators.goal: Specify the selected business behavior precisely enough to implement and independently accept it.

action.en: Resolve the canonical .work workspace and selected business leaf. Research accepted intent, domain documents and current FE/BE callers at exact revisions. Classify every citation as accepted intent, observed source, proposal or unknown; source behavior never approves policy. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers.

Write objective, glossary, actors, ownership, FR/BR and measurable NFRs. Separate output from persisted effects and technical constraints from business policy. Preserve unknown numeric targets with the decision owner; never invent targets.

Write ordered flows with entry, actor, prerequisites, request, response/error, transitions, guards, side effects and postconditions. Cover success, invalid/denied input, retry, duplicate, concurrency, cancellation and recovery where relevant; mark non-applicability with reasons.

Trace each flow to observed UI/API/module/store callers and affected services. Record a preliminary codeImpacts/serviceImpacts inventory, source citations, direct versus transitive impact, preserve/change/review disposition and unknowns. This is architecture input, not authorization to edit every discovered file.

Specify actor-action-resource permissions, tenant/owner boundaries, sensitive-data handling and abuse cases. Give each security requirement an observable denial/no-side-effect acceptance scenario; do not mistake a disabled UI control for server enforcement.

Assign stable requirement/flow/AC IDs and Given/When/Then expectations, proof owner and instrument. Record decisions to implement/preserve/defer/not-applicable with authority and revisit condition. Store the full JSON payload in extensions.work3.specification and real dependencies/refs in core fields, not hidden prose. Author canonical user journeys and journeyCoverage links to flow/AC IDs using the shared journey contract; preserve accepted journeys unchanged in architecture. Do not convert internal service hops into UI actions. Browser-free scope may use an empty array only when no UAT acceptance is assigned.

Validate coverage and .work bindings; review all unresolved decisions together. Output requirements, ordered flows, acceptance, preliminary impact and security inputs for architecture/draw/planning. No automatic secondary call is defined for this op; report a missing decision and do not invent a helper. Complete only this reviewed business scope. When selected in a job matrix, produce E/job-result.json bound to the exact request, its output schema and every required criterion. This handoff is conditional and does not change standalone or named frontend response contracts.

operators.goal: Create or revise one selected content unit with grounded claims and actual requested media/code checks.

action.en: Resolve requested audience/outcomes, edition/locale, factual constraints and source-owned paths. A new content-only workspace can use explicitly selected deliverable paths, not a fabricated product repository. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers.
Write or revise only selected content and examples, preserving correct existing material and linking nontrivial factual claims to actual sources. Label illustrative examples.

Generate requested assets with available appropriate skill/tools and inspect them; run executable examples and declared builds when selected, retain actual outputs. Unrequested media/language variants are not mandatory.
Review outcome coverage, clarity, factuality, source rights and locale consistency. Independent review requires actual authorized reviewer; self-review is labelled honestly.

Commit selected tracked content when authorized or report local deliverables/uncommitted result accurately. Stop without publishing or changing curriculum outside scope. When selected in a job matrix, produce E/job-result.json bound to the exact request, its output schema and every required criterion. This handoff is conditional and does not change standalone or named frontend response contracts.

operators.goal: Produce and inspect the requested visual direction for one business-grounded surface.

action.en: Freeze the selected brief and content/region mapping, labelling placeholder/example copy. Choose a code-native/vector or raster medium matching the request; do not force ImageGen where not appropriate. Map the canonical accepted journeys and required screens/states/viewports to the complete planned draws array. Ground existing components in source; greenfield surfaces remain proposed. Check architecture service/API boundaries before representing actions. Own the screen/content plan inside this draw job: specify shell, responsive states, truthful landing-page claims, region and asset ownership, motion/accessibility constraints and transitions before producing images. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers. Identify reusable and missing visual assets in the direction. Codex working profiles may use an actually available image generator. Claude may render code-native layouts and reserve blank decorative artwork slots with briefs for later drawing; never claim missing raster artwork was generated. Actual reviewed layout images are still required by the draw output contract.
Use the available appropriate tool/skill to create the requested direction; retain the actual output and provenance. Missing tool means blocked output, never a claimed generated image.

Open and inspect actual output for business contradictions, hierarchy, component ownership, legibility, responsive feasibility and each independent asset. Distinguish subjective judgement from measured geometry. Review every image against applicable knowledge and mapped journey states; record actual coverage and unresolved conflicts. Never pass a mandatory state using an unrelated representative image.

Present the actual direction. Reuse accepted choice; ask only if materially different alternatives were requested and selection remains open. Stop without frontend code. For workflow execution, Return outputs.draws as the full reviewed image array with artifact IDs and screen/state/viewport mapping. Submit the exact response to the coordinator gate; never self-advance. Write E/draws.json for FE delivery in standalone and workflow modes; include every required reviewed image and retain its real artifact bytes. When selected in a job matrix, produce E/job-result.json bound to the exact request, its output schema and every required criterion. This handoff is conditional and does not change standalone or named frontend response contracts.

operators.goal: Implement one selected frontend creation, refinement or defect repair by reconciling the full draws image array, business intent, architecture and current source, then verify the actual rendered result.

action.en: Collect the selected scope, business ACs, architecture/API contracts, current source and applicable knowledge. Validate draws as an array and open every image; index each by actual screen/state/viewport and source identity in draws-review and the input map. Resolve shared layouts, responsive variants, sequential states and ambiguous alternatives explicitly. For repairs reproduce the original defect and preserve its evidence. Own preparation through delivery: inspect readiness and reproduce the requested defect when applicable, partition the selected work into cohesive changes and check callers before editing. Resolve repository-local dependencies and bounded development runtime needs under the existing scope. Shared library changes belong to the actual FE or BE package owner: include owner tests, packaging/export compatibility and selected consumer integration proof in this same implementation; never publish a package implicitly. Keep shared paths exclusive and report a missing required external authority rather than inventing a helper. For a landing surface, implement the accepted content, section sequence, assets and responsive interaction in the selected frontend source. Draw is only needed when the request requires a new visual decision; do not add a mandatory planning predecessor. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers.

Map every relevant region across all draws to routes, shared/owned components, API reads/actions, states, ACs and actual knowledge rules/cases. Business governs behavior; images express accepted visual intent within applicable knowledge and installed component constraints. Record missing screens/states and cross-image or knowledge conflicts; do not average incompatible alternatives, invent behavior from pictures or weaken the selected graph.

Implement the mapped screens and shared layout once using actual installed components, tokens and repository conventions. Apply scoped creation, refinement or the smallest defect repair; retain cross-image consistency, responsive behavior, keyboard and focus. Follow applicable knowledge even where literal image copying would violate it; unresolved material design conflicts remain blocked. Account for every asset visible in every input draw. Reuse a verified matching asset or create/generate the required asset, inspect it and integrate its actual source file. Claude with no image-generation capability may reserve a blank decorative slot with a deferred brief; never use invented URLs, broken images or label pending art complete. Functional asset requirements remain blocking. Record E/assets.json even when the reviewed draws need no distinct assets.

Connect actual data reads/actions, validation, permissions and navigation for the mapped journeys. Implement applicable loading, empty, error, denied, success and recovery states from the accepted business/API contracts, including required states not depicted in draws. Never guess endpoints, fake success or invent undisclosed business decisions. CALL POINT (step 4): if an observed API integration or render-data defect blocks an already accepted journey and is repairable without business changes, read interface.implement/secondary.json and call its listed backend.implement role. Pass the exact backend repository, allowed file paths, defect evidence/problem, changeKind and unchanged businessRefs. Set FE to waiting in this same cell. If no such defect exists, skip this call. If the repair needs business/schema/authorization changes or an unlisted operator, return blocked with the missing decision. Resume this step only after every required support response matches its request and passes every required criterion in the caller-owned secondary.json, including scope, business preservation, API compatibility, implementation quality and commit verification; inspect returned changes, integrate the actual commits and continue to step 5. Defects discovered in steps 5 or 6 return to this call point under the same permissions; never create an implicit helper.

Run relevant component/unit, interaction, type, lint and build checks for mapped ACs/states and applicable knowledge. For repairs retain before/after evidence for the original unchanged expected assertion plus collateral regressions. Fix only within scope; keep failed or untested required behavior visible. This implement op owns lint, typecheck, relevant tests/coverage, affected builds and Sonar. Resolve real repository scripts and CI thresholds; record command, source tree/commit, result and sanitized logs. For Sonar record the analysis/revision and actual server quality-gate result after processing; scanner submission alone is not pass. Fix scoped failures and rerun affected checks. A missing runner, token reference, coverage target or unavailable required Sonar gate is blocked/not-run, never pass; do not move this responsibility to architecture, business or UAT. Reuse existing authorization and keep secrets outside evidence.

Bind an authorized preview and observed served build. Open the implemented screens, drive relevant controls and capture every required screen/state/viewport represented by draws plus other required acceptance states. Open the captures and compare each mapped draw with its corresponding rendered evidence and applicable knowledge rules. Record coverage per input image and all deviations; no representative screenshot may stand in for unobserved screens. Repair within scope and recheck affected tests/captures before passing.

Review the owned diff and complete draws/AC/state/rule coverage; account for every input image and preserve justified out-of-scope limitations without silently dropping requirements. Record actual code commits when authorized, tested/served revisions, evidence and remaining gaps. Complete only when required implementation and rendered proof pass. Independent full UAT remains separate; stop. For workflow execution, Return outputs.flows in the original journey order, preserving business actions/expectations and adding actual sourcePaths; return full codeRefs including accepted backend support commits and the verified rendered runtime. These outputs become UAT inputs unchanged. Submit the exact response to the coordinator gate; never self-advance. Create the scoped local commit under the existing implementation authority after required checks pass, read back full SHA and committed diff, and return per-repository commit references. Preserve unrelated local changes; never stage everything, bypass hooks, push or invent an empty commit. If no code changed, return the verified existing commit and explain no change. Missing commit proof prevents a passing delivery. Always write E/flows.json as the ready UAT handoff, even outside a named workflow; preserve accepted journey order and expected results, bind source paths, real commits and the observed served build. Validate with validateFEHandoff against the selected accepted journeys before delivery. When selected in a job matrix, produce E/job-result.json bound to the exact request, its output schema and every required criterion. This handoff is conditional and does not change standalone or named frontend response contracts. Include assets in E/flows.json and FE outputs alongside flows/codeRefs/runtime; pass the exact manifest to UAT. The assets-accounted-for criterion requires full draw coverage and real ready assets or explicitly allowed decorative deferrals.

operators.goal: Repair one challenged canonical instruction/rule and affected references from concrete applicability evidence.

action.en: Check whether the issue is existing enforcement failure, missing concept, wrong existing rule or duplicate concept using the actual maintenance policy of the selected owner. Choose one canonical owner before edits. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers.

Make smallest scoped rule/gate/step repair with stable IDs, same-commit affected reference updates and no product-specific law. Update genuine callers/contracts together; do not patch consumers as hidden workaround.

Run actual relevant validation/citation/parity and behavioral regression checks. Generated documents use their owned generators; inspect changes rather than claiming textual shape proves sound guidance.

Commit owned change when authorized and report exact originating context needing re-evaluation. Do not automatically rerun its operation or claim visual correctness. When selected in a job matrix, produce E/job-result.json bound to the exact request, its output schema and every required criterion. This handoff is conditional and does not change standalone or named frontend response contracts.

operators.goal: Deliver one explicitly selected publication, deployment or database migration and verify its exact remote outcome.

action.en: Resolve the exact named operation and load only its contract. Its reads/writes, effect ceiling and completion profile replace this selector envelope; the union of modes never grants authority. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers.

Execute the selected mode procedure through its actual postconditions. Return operation, scope, per-criterion results and real output refs; no other mode, source repair or successor is implied. When selected in a job matrix, produce E/job-result.json bound to the exact request, its output schema and every required criterion. This handoff is conditional and does not change standalone or named frontend response contracts.

operators.goal: Independently verify a selected delivery, business, workflow, rendered visual or API result without repairing its producer.

action.en: Resolve the exact named operation and load only its contract. Its reads/writes, effect ceiling and completion profile replace this selector envelope; the union of modes never grants authority. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers.

Execute the selected mode procedure through its actual postconditions. Return operation, scope, per-criterion results and real output refs; no other mode, source repair or successor is implied. When selected in a job matrix, produce E/job-result.json bound to the exact request, its output schema and every required criterion. This handoff is conditional and does not change standalone or named frontend response contracts.

operators.goal: Deliver the requested runtime or service state with readiness, owned effects and real postcondition proof.

action.en: Resolve the exact named operation and load only its contract. Its reads/writes, effect ceiling and completion profile replace this selector envelope; the union of modes never grants authority. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers.

Execute the selected mode procedure through its actual postconditions. Return operation, scope, per-criterion results and real output refs; no other mode, source repair or successor is implied. When selected in a job matrix, produce E/job-result.json bound to the exact request, its output schema and every required criterion. This handoff is conditional and does not change standalone or named frontend response contracts.

operators.goal: Retire exactly the selected business/resource scope while preserving required evidence and live consumers.

action.en: Inventory exact selected nodes/resources, Git state, image/evidence/account custody references and all live consumers. Distinguish custom durable .worktrees artifacts from Git-managed checkouts. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers.
Resolve consumer preserve/replace/defer/retire dispositions and retention/recovery obligations. Missing decision or custody blocks deletion, not the read-only inventory.

Verify required durable artifacts are retained and retrievable at approved destinations before any explicitly selected deletion. Resolve absolute targets, symlink/junction boundaries and worktree registration; never broad recursive delete a workspace/root.

Execute only separately authorized exact retirement effects, preferring reversible operations and appropriate Git worktree lifecycle. Preserve uncommitted/untracked user work; uncertain ownership stops removal.

Validate surviving references/readability and report what was retired, actually removed, retained and recoverable. Stop; no opportunistic cleanup of adjacent work. When selected in a job matrix, produce E/job-result.json bound to the exact request, its output schema and every required criterion. This handoff is conditional and does not change standalone or named frontend response contracts.

operators.goal: Discover, execute and verify one concrete request directly when no specialized workflow fits, without assuming domain knowledge and routes missing Work through the approved bootstrap workflow.

action.en: Turn the request into one bounded job: desired outcome, known inputs, exact effect ceiling, acceptance criteria and current unknowns. Use available working tools. For unclear details, inspect first and ask only decisions that materially change the intended result or mutation target.

Research just enough actual context to act correctly: source ownership/call chain and reproduction for a fix; immutable artifact and target state for a deployment; actual schema, keys and pre-update rows for data correction. Identify existing partial effects before retries. Do not require business/architecture/Work setup ops as prerequisites.

Choose the smallest plan that completes the requested job, including appropriate checks and recoverability. Resolve exact source paths, target rows/resources and predicates before mutation. Data corrections need attributable IDs, read-back and a transaction or explicit recoverable method when available. Deployment needs the selected target/artifact and bounded health/rollback checks. Missing material authority blocks only the affected action.

Perform the selected change with the observed instruments and existing authorization. Reuse correct behavior and artifacts. Keep changes scoped; do not sweep unrelated files, reset worktrees, bypass hooks, publish or alter production data outside the request. After uncertain remote results reconcile by read-back before retry. Do not invoke another op or restart a workflow implicitly.

Verify the actual outcome against every original criterion. For source changes run the relevant discovered repository checks and regressions; for deployment verify the running artifact/health; for data changes read back exact records and affected invariants. Repair scoped failures within a finite plan without weakening criteria. Preserve partial effects and recovery failures honestly; a clean command exit alone is insufficient.

Return result, evidence, effects and remaining as declared by the direct-task cell, with exact request binding, statuses and real artifact refs. Record actual commits where applicable. Pass only when required criteria and effect read-back pass; otherwise fail/blocked with remaining work. Stop after this job. An ad hoc result is not implicit product UAT, business approval or completion of an unrelated Work tree.

operators.goal: Execute the requested sequential UX flows with scoped account/seed setup, real screenshot/video evidence and verified cleanup.

action.en: Freeze the requested flows order, business expectations and applicable UX checks before effects. UX answers are yes/no for observed loading feedback, error feedback, skeleton, validation, retry/recovery and completion as requested; no beauty, spacing, color, typography or visual-fidelity scoring. Specify expected yes or no and applicability before running; a skeleton is not universally required and no error on a happy path is not automatically a failure. Verify runtime/served identity and actual screenshot/video capability before starting. Own case preparation within this invocation: map every requested flow and step to accepted ACs, actor, entry, preconditions, feedback, persistent read-back where required, real screenshot/video checkpoints and cleanup obligations before effects. Locator choices never redefine expected behavior. No plan/account/seed predecessor is required. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers. Read the FE asset manifest and preserve explicit deferred artwork status. Test business/UX expectations only; cosmetic artwork may remain pending under the accepted profile policy, but missing assets required by a requested flow cannot satisfy its criteria.

Inspect or author the missing seed/delete/resource-management scripts from actual owners. Review dry-run targets and failure behavior, test their guards without destructive product effects, and prepare a finally-style cleanup path before the first mutation. The run ledger records reused baselines and every created/mutated ID immediately; discover unknown provider outcomes by read-only correlation before retries.

Reuse a suitable account or create the authorized scoped account through its supported provider/script; verify actual login, role and membership. Resolve credentials at use time and isolate browser sessions for distinct actors while retaining the session continuity each sequential flow requires. Track disposable account ownership separately from reused identities.

Execute reviewed parameterized seed SQL only for missing prerequisites, recording exact inserted IDs and before-images for any authorized changes to reused records. Verify preconditions by read-back. Finalize identity/fixture metadata and compute the actual verification digest before starting the tested journeys; never seed a successful outcome or fabricate a passing prerequisite.

Run flows[0], flows[1], and so on in the requested order, each action in its declared sequence, with real browser controls and continuous real video per flow. Capture screenshots at significant steps, loading/error/skeleton observations and failure points. Real configured paid AI calls are permitted within the authorized flow; do not substitute mocked AI success. Record asynchronous operation/resource IDs promptly and verify actual completion, not merely request acceptance.

For each reached checkpoint answer observed UX checks yes/no only, linked to screenshot/video timestamps. Verify expected business results through actual response, reload/resume and authorized read-only API/SQL read-back; API writes never perform an action claimed as UI-tested. Preserve failures; dependent later steps are not-run, while independent later flows may proceed only in original order with safe preconditions. Do not repair product code or rewrite expected outcomes inside UAT.

After success, failure or interruption, finalize and inspect the real recordings/screens and run the prepared cleanup for all owned effects. Delete externally provisioned resources through the supported direct provider/API script using exact ledger IDs before removing local metadata; SQL deletion alone cannot delete a VM or stop billing. Poll/reconcile actual absence or provider deletion completion and dependent owned resources. Run cleanup SQL in dependency-safe order, restore authorized reused-record before-images and remove disposable accounts only when owned and selected for cleanup. Preserve shared/reused objects and explicitly retained prerequisites; never broad-delete by age or name prefix alone.

Read back database and provider state to prove cleanup, retaining the ownership ledger, scripts and sanitized evidence. If a resource remains, record exact IDs, costs when observable and an executable resume-cleanup command; incomplete cleanup blocks overall done even when flows passed. Report each flow result, the yes/no UX table, screenshot/video refs, usage/cost observations and cleanup result. Validate bound evidence and stop; never claim the journey succeeded solely because cleanup succeeded. For workflow execution, Return outputs.results for every input flow and step in order, yes/no UX observations and screenshot/video evidence, plus outputs.cleanup with no unresolved owned resources for a pass. Submit the exact response to the coordinator gate; never self-advance. When selected in a job matrix, produce E/job-result.json bound to the exact request, its output schema and every required criterion. This handoff is conditional and does not change standalone or named frontend response contracts.

operators.goal: Create or reconstruct one canonical .work workspace from a new purpose or selected existing source and old worktrees, with verified bindings, preserved provenance and validated scope.

action.en: Select prepare for a new or explicitly revised Work purpose, or import for an existing source/worktree pilot. Resolve one canonical destination, then load exactly that operation contract.
